title.en: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail
title.zh: 巴基斯坦最高法院命令将前总理伊姆兰·汗从监狱转送医院

summary.en: Imran Khan, Pakistan's former prime minister, has been ordered by the country's top court to be moved from jail to a hospital. He has been imprisoned since 2023 on corruption charges, which he claims are politically motivated.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦最高法院下令将前总理伊姆兰·汗从监狱转移到医院。他自2023年以来一直因腐败指控被监禁，但他声称这些指控是出于政治动机。

body.en:
Pakistan's Supreme Court has ordered jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be moved to hospital, following complaints about his poor health.

A three-judge panel ordered that the cricketer-turned-politician be taken to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad in the next 48 hours to be examined by physicians.

The court also said Khan would be allowed weekly meetings with family members and telephone calls with his sons.

Khan has been imprisoned since 2023 on corruption charges, which he says were politically motivated.

In Tuesday's court order, the panel wrote: "We are mindful of the constitutional and legal obligation... to safeguard the life, health, dignity and security of the prisoner."

The 73-year-old's lawyers have said he's suffering from various health conditions, including poor eyesight, and has been unable to access specialist medical care.

In February, Khan's lawyer said his client had 15% vision left in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action - an allegation the government disputed.

Reacting to the ruling, Zulfikar Bukhari, an adviser to Khan, said in quotes cited by AFP news agency: "We wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much".

The court order said an eye specialist would be involved in Khan's hospital treatment.

The judges and members of Khan's political party, Tehreek-e-Insaf, have warned supporters not to gather outside the hospital when he is transferred there, which would be a breach of the court order.

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as the country's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

He was imprisoned in August 2023 and has faced charges in more than 100 cases, ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts - all of which he decried as politically motivated.

His jailing triggered large-scale protests by supporters, which were met with a crackdown by authorities.

Despite his jailing, Khan remains a significant presence in Pakistani politics with a large number of supporters.
body.zh: 巴基斯坦最高法院下令将被监禁的前总理伊姆兰·汗转移到医院，因为有人抱怨他的健康状况不佳。 一个由三名法官组成的小组下令在接下来的 48 小时内将这位板球运动员转为政治家的人送往伊斯兰堡的希法国际医院接受医生检查。 法院还表示，汗将被允许每周与家人会面并与儿子们打电话。 汗自 2023 年以来一直因腐败指控而入狱，他说这些指控是出于政治动机。 在周二的法院命令中，专家组写道：“我们铭记宪法和法律义务……保护囚犯的生命、健康、尊严和安全。” 这位 73 岁老人的律师表示，他患有多种健康问题，包括视力不佳，并且无法获得专业医疗护理。 今年 2 月，汗的律师表示，由于监狱当局未能采取行动，他的当事人的右眼视力只剩下 15%，但政府对这一指控提出了异议。 法新社援引汗的顾问佐尔菲卡尔·布哈里(Zulfikar Bukhari)对这一裁决的反应说：“我们希望这件事早点发生，这样他的眼睛和总体健康状况就不会恶化得这么严重。” 法院命令称，一名眼科专家将参与汗的医院治疗。 法官和汗所在政党 Tehreek-e-Insaf 的成员警告支持者，当他被转移到医院时，不要聚集在医院外，否则将违反法院命令。 汗曾担任巴基斯坦国家板球队队长，并于 2018 年至 2022 年担任该国总理。 他于 2023 年 8 月入狱，面临 100 多起案件的指控，从泄露国家机密到出售国家礼品，他谴责所有这些都是出于政治动机。 他的入狱引发了支持者的大规模抗议，但遭到当局镇压。 尽管被监禁，汗仍然在巴基斯坦政坛发挥着重要作用，拥有大量支持者。

reflection.en: This news highlights the critical role of judicial bodies in upholding justice and ensuring humane treatment, even for those accused of serious crimes. Yahweh calls those in authority to do justice and righteousness, protecting individuals from harm and ensuring their well-being.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了司法机构在维护正义和确保人道待遇方面的关键作用，即使是对被指控犯有严重罪行的人。雅伟呼召掌权者行公义、好怜悯，保护个人免受伤害并确保他们的福祉。

verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Afghanistan: Only 5% of labor market are women under Taliban
title.zh: 阿富汗：塔利班统治下女性仅占劳动力市场的 5%

summary.en: The International Labour Organization estimates that only 5.1% of workers in Afghanistan are women, five years after the Taliban's return to power. That's less than a third of the proportion in 2019 and 2020.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 国际劳工组织估计，塔利班重新掌权五年后，阿富汗工人中只有 5.1% 是女性。这还不到 2019 年和 2020 年比例的三分之一。 根据国际劳工组织 (ILO) 周二发布的一份报告，自塔利班重新掌权以来的五年里，阿富汗劳动力市场中女性的比例已下降至每 20 人中就有 1 人左右。 国际劳工组织写道：“在妇女接受教育和就业的机会受到严格限制的背景下，阿富汗的女性劳动力参与率预计在全球第二低，到 2026 年仅为 5.1%。” 它呼吁采取紧急措施应对妇女的“严重排斥”，并表示这对于增强阿富汗经济的整体弹性至关重要。 随着美国和其他北约部队撤军，塔利班于 2021 年 8 月迅速重新掌权，结束了妇女在多年的伊斯兰强硬统治后享有相对改善的经济和教育自由的 20 年时期。 该联合国组织警告说，自 2021 年以来，劳动力市场将发生“重大的人口和制度变化”，其中许多变化使女性处于不利地位。 国际劳工组织阿富汗办事处主任兼高级协调员蒂特·哈比亚卡雷 (Tite Habiyakare) 表示：“在如此大比例的人口仍被排除在经济活动之外的情况下，阿富汗无法建立一个有弹性的劳动力市场。” 报告称，塔利班接管五年后，阿富汗劳动力市场仍“承受相当大的压力”，仅从 2021 年的崩溃中略有恢复。 当塔利班在新冠病毒大流行期间卷土重来以及西方军队和资金外流时，阿富汗的 GDP 下降了约 15%。 2022 年，该数字仍深陷负值区域，此后才勉强进入正增长区域，远未恢复到塔利班之前的水平。 从绝对值来看，就业人数已经开始上升，但速度还不够快，无法跟上人口增长的速度——无论是国内人口还是移民回国造成的——这意味着工作人口的比例正趋于平稳，仅占总人口的不到三分之一。 该文件还呼吁增加对代表性劳动力数据收集的投资，并警告说，其数据依赖于模型估计，而模型估计“存在相当大的不确定性，应谨慎解释”。 报告称，移民，特别是来自伊朗和巴基斯坦的移民的大规模回返，已成为“阿富汗面临的劳动力市场的决定性挑战之一”。 2023年至今年5月底，已有超过600万阿富汗人从伊朗和巴基斯坦返回...

title.en: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
title.zh: 独居休达街头的未成年人面临虐待风险

summary.en: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

It's 8 a.m. at the Tarajal industrial park in the autonomous city of Ceuta. But there are no workers and truck drivers to be seen near the warehouses today. Instead, there are makeshift tents, some of them made out of cardboard, with mainly children and teenagers sleeping under dirty blankets.

According to certain estimates, there could be between 3,000 and 5,000 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta. Some are living on the streets because they cannot find a spot in one of the already overcrowded reception facilities in the enclave.

Amina (not her real name), a 14-year-old Moroccan girl, and her brother were among the 80,000 people who crossed the border into Spain from Morocco in late July. Though most of these have since left Ceuta , some 9,000 remain, according to the local authorities — and many are minors. "

What's worst is that we don't have toilets," said Amina. "We have to go somewhere in the bushes, but I don't dare go alone."

Close by is a Moroccan woman called Malika (also not her real name) who has spread out several blankets for herself and her four children. She told DW she was not making enough as a cleaning lady in Morocco , adding that she earned the equivalent of €7 ($8) per day.

"That's just not enough to provide for everyone," she said. "School will start again soon, and I don't have any money for books, nor even decent clothes for the children."

That's why she decided to take part in the mass crossing of the Spanish border last month when she read about it on social media. But now she doesn't know what to do.

"One child got sick. He had a high fever, but I couldn't get help anywhere," she said. In the end, she made compresses with water and vinegar to see if that would help.

But now she is particularly worried about her 12-and 14-year-old daughters, because the number of sexual assaults has risen sharply in the past week. Police are currently investigating at least 15 suspected cases of rape. The local authorities suspect the actual number of cases to be much higher.

Susana Ascaso, an emergency doctor at Ceuta University Hospital, said she had treated several young girls in recent days.

"Just yesterday, another 12-year-old came to the emergency room," she said. "She said that other migrants had harassed her and touched her inappropriately. She arrived here completely terrified and in tears. She was with a woman who had found her on the street. That woman saved the girl."

body.zh: 数千名无人陪伴的未成年人聚集在非洲北海岸的西班牙飞地休达。疾病和虐待盛行，当局承认他们不知所措。 上午 8 点，位于休达自治市的塔拉哈尔工业园区。但今天仓库附近没有看到工人和卡车司机。相反，有临时帐篷，其中一些是用纸板制成的，主要是儿童和青少年睡在肮脏的毯子下。 据估计，休达可能有 3,000 至 5,000 名无人陪伴的未成年人。有些人流落街头，因为他们在飞地已经人满为患的接待设施中找不到一席之地。 阿米娜（化名）是一名 14 岁的摩洛哥女孩，她和她的兄弟是 7 月底从摩洛哥越过边境进入西班牙的 8 万人中的一员。据当地政府称，尽管其中大多数人已经离开休达，但仍有约 9,000 人留下，其中许多人是未成年人。 ” 最糟糕的是我们没有厕所，”阿米娜说。 “我们必须去灌木丛里的某个地方，但我不敢一个人去。” 附近是一位名叫马利卡（Malika）（也不是她的真名）的摩洛哥妇女，她为自己和四个孩子铺好了几条毯子。她告诉德国之声，她在摩洛哥做清洁工赚的钱不够多，并补充说她每天的收入相当于 7 欧元（8 美元）。 “这还不足以养活所有人，”她说。 “学校马上就要开学了，我没有钱买书，甚至没有钱给孩子们穿像样的衣服。” 这就是为什么她上个月在社交媒体上看到有关大规模穿越西班牙边境的报道后决定参加这一活动。但现在她不知道该怎么办。 “一个孩子生病了。他发高烧，但我无法在任何地方获得帮助，”她说。最后，她用水和醋做了敷布，看看是否有帮助。 但现在她特别担心自己12岁和14岁的女儿，因为过去一周性侵犯的数量急剧上升。警方目前正在调查至少15起疑似强奸案。地方当局怀疑实际病例数要高得多。 休达大学医院的急诊医生苏珊娜·阿斯卡索说，她最近几天治疗了几名年轻女孩。 “就在昨天，另一名 12 岁的孩子来到急诊室，”她说。 “她说其他移民骚扰了她，并对她进行了不恰当的触摸。她到达这里时非常害怕，流着泪。她和一名在街上发现她的妇女在一起。那个妇女救了这个女孩。” 阿斯卡索表示，对于“18 岁以下的女孩”来说，情况尤其困难，她们“尤其面临风险”。她补充说，存在着严重的不平衡……

title.en: Should India be worried about the Mecca defense pact?
title.zh: 印度是否应该担忧麦加防务协议？

summary.en: A new defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey is integrating Pakistan more deeply into the Middle East's security framework. This development raises questions about how India will react to the evolving geopolitical landscape.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦、沙特阿拉伯和土耳其之间的一项新防务协议，使巴基斯坦更深入地融入中东的安全架构。这一发展引发了人们对印度将如何应对不断变化的地区局势的疑问。

body.en:
A defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey brings Islamabad deeper into the security architecture of the Middle East. How is India planning to respond?

The "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on August 7, comes amid the Iran war and shifting security arrangements in the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia is seeking additional security partnerships amid uncertainty over the reliability of the US security umbrella. Turkey is seeking a larger regional role, while Pakistan is looking to turn its longstanding military relationship with Riyadh into wider strategic influence.

The agreement calls for collective defense, stating an armed attack on one member will be regarded as an attack on all three.

It also formalizes relationships that already exist . Pakistan has trained and assisted Saudi forces for decades, while its defense relationship with Turkey has expanded through military exchanges and cooperation.

For India , the question is whether the pact gives arch-rival Pakistan a deeper role in a region central to Indian interests.

Some Indian analysts see little immediate change in the regional balance. Others see a warning that India needs a stronger security presence in a region where its economic interests have grown considerably.

Saudi Arabia is a major energy and investment partner for New Delhi. The Gulf and the Red Sea are vital to India's trade and energy security.

The pact allows Pakistan to expand on its security role in the Gulf while providing an institutional framework for closer defense cooperation and potentially greater access to funding and technology.

However, former Indian High Commissioner to Pakistan Ajay Bisaria believes the agreement will have little effect on the basic dynamics of an India Pakistan confrontation.

"It does little to move the needle beyond the Saudi-Pakistan defense pact of last year, an arrangement that proved to have only signaling value for Iran, the US and Israel, at a moment when Riyadh was unsettled by the frailty of the American security umbrella," he added.

In the event of a future India Pakistan crisis, the former ambassador said he does not expect the pact to fundamentally alter Saudi Arabia's position.

"For India, this is a pact to be monitored, not one to be unduly concerned about," Bisaria said.

"In the event of another terrorist attack from Pakistan, the situation is unlikely to look very different from Operation Sindoor, save, perhaps, for some added rhetoric," he said, referring to the name of India's response to a 2025 attack on tourists in Kashmir that New Delhi blames on Pakistan-backed militants . Islamabad denies any involvement in the attack.

title.en: Brazil's President Lula hails oil discovery near Amazon river
title.zh: 巴西总统卢拉称赞亚马逊河附近发现石油

summary.en: Environmentalists have heavily criticised the exploratory drilling in the sea off the mouth of the Amazon.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has hailed the discovery of oil near the mouth of the Amazon river.

Speaking after the find was announced by Brazil's state-run oil company Petrobras, he said it could be "a passport to the country's future".

His decision to allow exploratory drilling in the area known as the Brazilian Equatorial Margin was heavily criticised by environmentalists, who raised concerns that any potential oil spills could devastate its ecosystem.

Lula, who is running for another four-year term in elections scheduled for October, stressed that he was still committed to eventually phasing out fossil fuels to curb climate change.

The oil discovery was made in the sea about 175km (110 miles) off the Amazon coast but the size of the field is not yet clear.

It is also still unknown whether extracting the oil, which is located at a depth of 2,886m (9,469ft), would be commercially viable.

Conservationists have warned that the area where the exploratory drilling is taking place is very biodiverse.

They fear that any accidents could threaten not just the nearby reefs but that currents could carry spilled oil to coastal wetlands teeming with wildlife.

Lula has in the past rejected criticism by conservationists as "meddling" and on Monday he again said that he would not accept any foreign interference.

"This means national sovereignty. Any country which has oil of this quality won't allow anyone to butt in," he said.

Petrobras started the exploratory deep-water drilling operation in the area in October 2025.

The company's chief executive Magda Chambriard said that the discovery confirmed that Petrobras's "optimism" of finding oil in the Brazilian Equatorial Margin had been warranted.

She added that the company was committed to "ensuring the country's energy security".

President Lula has argued that oil revenues are needed to help fund Brazil's transition to non-fossil fuels.

Speaking on Monday, he insisted: "I'm not denying my commitment to the fight for a day when we no longer need fossil fuels, because Brazil will continue to be the king of biofuel innovation and will remain a major player in renewable energy."

Environmentalists were aghast when Lula announced he had given Petrobras the green light to start the exploratory drilling just weeks before the COP30 climate conference hosted by Brazil last November.

In his remarks on Monday, the president made a reference to the anger at the time, singling out opposition in Europe in particular.

"Many people didn't want me to announce that Petrobras had won the licence because they said that the Europeans would be annoyed," he said.

title.en: UK 'supports Ukraine 100%', Burnham says, after Russia's drone warning
title.zh: 俄罗斯就英国向乌克兰提供无人机发出警告

summary.en: Russia has issued a warning to the UK regarding its supply of drones to Ukraine. In response, a UK Ministry of Defence spokesperson stated that Britain stands "shoulder to shoulder" with Ukraine.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯就英国向乌克兰提供无人机一事向英国发出警告。英国国防部发言人回应称，英国与乌克兰“并肩作战”。

body.en:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said London will continue "to support Ukraine 100%", after Moscow warned of "consequences" following confirmation that British-made drones were used in recent Ukrainian strikes in Russia.

"We are not fair-weather friends, we will be there in Ukraine's hour of need and that won't change," he said.

The Russian embassy in the UK earlier accused Britain of "deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis", saying "the deeper its involvement in the conflict... the higher the price it will pay".

Kyiv has stepped up long-range attacks on Moscow and other Russian regions, targeting oil refineries and warehouses of the largest online retailer Wildberries.

Asked on Tuesday about the Russian threat, Burnham maintained that the UK was "providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself and that's been the British position all the way through this conflict, by previous prime ministers - it remains the case with me".

This is not the first time that Russia has warned the UK over its role in providing Ukraine with drone technology and Storm Shadow missiles .

The Russian embassy said "London's actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer", but did not elaborate on the type of threat Moscow was considering.

The latest phase of the war has directly affected Russia's domestic fuel supplies and dented the Russian economy.

The UK has been one of Ukraine's biggest international supporters since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Ministry of Defence said the UK was "committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's illegal invasion".

Two British companies are known to have built drones supplied to Kyiv . A military source confirmed to the BBC that UK drones had been used in recent attacks on Russia that reportedly caused more than £35bn in economic damage.

The Kremlin has regularly singled out the UK - along with the US - for its role in arming and backing Kyiv politically and financially since the start of the war.

It was London - then under Boris Johnson's leadership - that supplied Ukraine with very effective anti-tank weapons that helped to stop Moscow's advance on Kyiv in the first few weeks of the war.

The UK has since provided more modern weaponry and has also been actively training Ukrainian soldiers. In July, Burnham showed that Britain's support would continue by making his first international visit as prime minister to Kyiv.

On Russia's state TV channels, the anti-UK rhetoric has intensified in recent weeks, with invited experts and lawmakers regularly calling for strikes against the UK.

body.zh: 在确认英国制造的无人机被用于袭击俄罗斯目标后，俄罗斯指责英国“故意选择升级乌克兰危机”。 俄罗斯驻英国大使馆在一份声明中写道：“英国这样做，是血腥犯罪和恐怖袭击的共犯和共犯。” 声明称，“伦敦的行动将不可避免地带来后果，必须对此做出回应”，并补充说，其卷入冲突越深，“付出的代价就越高”。 作为回应，英国国防部发言人告诉英国广播公司新闻，英国与乌克兰“肩并肩”。 这位发言人在一份声明中表示：“俄罗斯应该毫不怀疑本届政府反对俄罗斯在乌克兰的侵略、反对英国和我们的盟友的决心。” 他们补充说，英国“致力于提供乌克兰所需的设备，以抵御俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的非法入侵”。 这些无人机由两家独立的英国公司制造，已在俄罗斯境内广泛成功地用于瞄准军事和工业目标，包括在线零售商 Wildberry 的炼油厂和仓库。 乌克兰多次针对这家被称为俄罗斯版亚马逊的公司，并表示最大的 Wildberry 物流中心中有十分之七已“瘫痪”。 一名军方消息人士向 BBC 证实，此次袭击使用了英国无人机，据称造成了超过 350 亿英镑的经济损失。 俄罗斯于2022年2月对乌克兰发动全面入侵，目前控制着乌克兰约五分之一的领土。 俄罗斯外交部发言人玛丽亚·扎哈罗娃表示，使用英国部件和配置的无人机被用来攻击俄罗斯领土，包括罗斯托夫地区卡缅斯基区的一个燃料库。 莫斯科向英国发出警告之前，乌克兰对俄罗斯发动了一波袭击，最近一次袭击发生在周一，造成 9 人死亡、23 人受伤，其中包括一名儿童。 乌克兰州长表示，周六晚上，乌克兰向俄罗斯发射了约 822 架无人机，其中 600 架瞄准莫斯科，俄罗斯首都遭受了“近期记忆中最大规模的无人机袭击之一”。俄罗斯各地报告有七人死亡。 当晚，俄罗斯对乌克兰发动袭击，造成至少7人死亡、超过39人受伤。 今年四月，国防部宣布将向乌克兰供应数万架无人机，其中包括远程打击装置，这是有史以来规模最大的一揽子计划。

Yahweh's word reminds us that those who live by the sword often face its consequences, urging reflection on the long-term impact of military aid. This dynamic underscores the need for wisdom in navigating geopolitical tensions, seeking paths...
reflection.zh: 俄罗斯和英国之间的交锋凸显了国际冲突中武装与警告的危险循环。雅伟的话语提醒我们，那些靠刀剑而活的人常常会面临其后果，促使我们反思军事援助的长期影响。这种动态强调了在处理地缘政治紧张局势时需要智慧，寻求避免暴力升级的道路。

title.en: Kariba ferry death toll rises to 93, making it Zimbabwe's deadliest transport disaster
title.zh: 卡里巴渡轮死亡人数上升至93人，成为津巴布韦最严重的交通灾难

summary.en: Recovery efforts continue in what is the country's deadliest transport disaster.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The death toll from a ferry disaster on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba has risen to 93, which makes it the country's deadliest transport disaster, according to the state-run Herald newspaper.

The ferry had a capacity to carry 90 passengers, but the paper estimates at least 168 people were actually on board when it was hit by a strong wave and overturned a week ago.

President Emmerson Mnangagwa declared a state of disaster following the accident and search and recovery efforts are continuing by divers.

The lake, which straddles the border with Zambia, is one of the world's largest man-made reservoirs, supporting transport and fishing and providing vital hydroelectric power to both countries.

The death toll rose from 44 at the time of the accident to 84 over the weekend, according to police.

Nine more bodies have since been found by divers and a police statement on Tuesday put the death toll at 93 , external .

The bodies were now being recovered further away from the scene of the sinking, some of them drifting towards Zambia, the Herald reports.

Provincial Affairs Minister Marian Chombo said 67 people had been rescued after the sinking.

But she added that it was proving difficult to identify some of the recovered bodies - with relatives having to rely on clothes and other items to do so.

"We are running out of time and DNA may now be needed to assist in the identification process," the minister was quoted by the Herald as saying.

The police said 83 of the victims had so far been identified, 39 of whom were children.

A vital and cheap transport link for rural communities, the ferry was carrying parents taking their children home for the school holidays and traders, the Herald said.

One survivor in her 40s told the AFP news agency that the ferry had been particularly overloaded at the time with goods - and passengers had raised concerns about the rough conditions.

"The life jackets were buried under the luggage, and not more than 30 people managed to get them," said Itayi Marumisa, a trader from Mola village.

"Children were screaming and most of the passengers were vomiting, but the captain did not seem to care."

A local councillor representing Mola, Tight Bhusumani, told the Herald it was a difficult time for his community, with children in particular affected.

"We have distressing cases where a child lost both parents and other siblings, leaving them as the only surviving member of the family," he is quoted as saying.

The councillor, who lost a child in the accident, said other families were still awaiting news of those believed to have been on the ferry.

title.en: These states have a united case against Meta. It could be social media's 'tobacco' moment
title.zh: 这些州联合起来反对 Meta。这可能是社交媒体的“烟草”时刻

summary.en: The trial's outcome could help reshape Facebook and Instagram, and leave Meta with billions of dollars to pay in penalties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As opening statements get underway in a landmark trial over claims that Meta Platforms misled the public about the safety of Instagram and Facebook for young users and violated child privacy laws, one of the biggest fights in the case has already been resolved: whether a bipartisan group of US states could present their claims together.

The states pushed for a single trial covering state consumer protection and federal privacy claims brought by 29 attorneys general, while Meta argued for a series of smaller trials grouping states that have similar laws.

The fight was about more than courtroom logistics. The states argued that the case centres on company-wide decisions affecting young users across the country and seeks nationwide changes to Meta's platforms, and that jurors should hear a single story about Meta's actions. Meta countered that jurors should evaluate states' claims separately because the underlying laws differ and warned that a combined proceeding could blur important distinctions among the claims.

Ultimately, US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers adopted a hybrid approach for the multi-week trial, allowing Colorado, California, Kentucky and New Jersey to try their state law claims together, while also including the federal law claims brought by all of the states. Although Rogers will decide the case, she appointed an advisory jury whose findings may inform her final ruling.

The trial's outcome could help guide how the remaining states' claims are resolved, reshape how Facebook and Instagram operate, and force Meta to pay billions of dollars in penalties.

Meta has called the allegations unsubstantiated and said it stands by its work to protect teen users of its platforms.

Legal experts said in a case against a company as well-capitalised as Meta, a multistate coalition gives the states the ability to pool resources and share expertise, and it may improve their credibility with the jury and the judge. They said attorneys general have used the strategy repeatedly in cases against the tobacco and opioid industries to strengthen their bargaining power and to present evidence of conduct that allegedly affected consumers across the country.

"A jury will see all these states banding together to do this, and that presents kind of like a projection of unity," said Prentiss Cox, a former assistant state attorney general in Minnesota who is now a law professor at the University of Minnesota Law School. “Elected officials on different sides of a partisan world can agree that this is a problem that needs solving.”

title.en: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history leaves 2,300 dead in Congo
title.zh: 历史上增长最快的埃博拉疫情在刚果造成 2,300 人死亡

summary.en: The World Health Organization has said the current Ebola outbreak is on track to surpass the deadliest on record.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak has now killed over 2,300 people and become the deadliest outbreak of the disease on record in the Central African nation.

The outbreak unfolding in one of DRC's most vulnerable regions is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever, with 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths, according to government data.

It's the DRC's 17th outbreak, with a toll that has eclipsed that of the country's 2018-2020 outbreak when 2,299 deaths out of 3,481 cases were recorded.

The latest data shows 101 new cases and 33 deaths reported in the previous 24 hours. Over 1,000 people have recovered, while 730 remain in hospitals or isolation.

The outbreak has infected and killed more people at a greater speed than any other outbreak in history. The World Health Organization has said it is on track to surpass the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, the deadliest on record with more than 11,000 deaths.

Trish Newport, emergency coordinator with Doctors Without Borders, said the limited community engagement in the outbreak remains a key challenge.

"The community needs to be aware about the outbreak," she told The Associated Press news agency, adding that people "need to be involved in the response, and they need to know what the signs and symptoms are and what to do if they get sick. And this today is not happening in every single place where there are Ebola cases".

Starting from the first confirmed case, the outbreak reached 2,000 killed almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 outbreak.

Some families have lost up to 15 of their relatives in the epicentre, the Ituri province, Newport said.

"We rapidly need to scale up to be able to prevent more deaths from happening, more families and communities from being impacted," she added.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current outbreak across six provinces in Congo's east. Trials for those are ongoing in Ituri.

Most new cases and deaths are being reported outside of the people being monitored. Challenges facing medical teams dealing with the outbreak also include strikes by some unpaid health workers, threats by rebel groups, anger from long-traumatised communities, bad roads making it difficult to reach all the affected territories, and misinformation claiming that Ebola isn’t real.

The WHO warned over the weekend that the outbreak is still moving at an "exceptional pace" ahead of efforts to track it, noting that it reached a weekly record of 579 cases and 304 deaths in the previous week.

title.en: Iran to go 'full offensive' if diplomacy fails as Trump threatens to bomb Oman
title.zh: 如果特朗普威胁轰炸阿曼，外交失败伊朗将“全面进攻”

summary.en: Iran has separately been negotiating an agreement with its neighbour Oman across the strait over managing Hormuz.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to its war with the United States have stalled, as the US ruled out extending a temporary ceasefire agreement.

Progress towards peace talks and a resumption of oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz has ground to a halt, with no sign that the warring parties are moving towards ending the conflict that the US and Israel launched with attacks on Iran on 28 February.

"Iranian entities must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region, as Iran will be ready to make decisions and take action on difficult decisions," a senior Iranian official told Reuters news agency.

The official added that Iran would conduct a "timely and precise" military attack to break the US naval blockade if diplomacy failed.

Monday marked the day Iran and the US were expected to reach a final peace agreement under a memorandum of understanding signed in June aimed at ending the war.

Signed on 17 June, the MoU set a 60-day timeframe for the US and Iran to reach a broader deal on Iran's nuclear program and US sanctions.

The agreement, which declared the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts", quickly unravelled over a dispute about control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the war.

Asked by reporters on Monday if the US was seeking to extend June's interim agreement, US President Donald Trump said no.

Iran said point 5 of the MoU gave it the right to manage the strait, which it shares with Oman, while the US rejected that interpretation. Hostilities resumed as Iran began firing on vessels it said were trying to sail through Hormuz on an unapproved route, and Trump said on 7 July that the pact was "over".

"Within the short period of a few weeks set by Iran, all the agreement's provisions must be implemented by the US. This is a precondition for further negotiations with the US," the Iranian official told Reuters, adding that mediators would share Iran's deadline with the US and regional countries.

Iran has been negotiating separately with its neighbour across the strait, Oman, to manage Hormuz, seen as a key component of a wider deal, and says it is close to an agreement, although progress has been slow.

title.en: China censors public mourning as it holds former premier's funeral
title.zh: 中国在举行前总理葬礼时审查公众哀悼活动

summary.en: While hailing Zhu’s legacy, authorities are wary that the nostalgia could lead to criticisms of Xi’s rule.

body.en:
Flags at government sites are flying at half-mast and security vehicles are parked in the heart of Beijing, as China mourns former Premier Zhu Rongji.

Zhu died of an illness last week at 97 and was cremated at a funeral in Beijing on Tuesday. The ceremony, attended by senior leaders including President Xi Jinping, was kept low-key. No footage has been released.

Zhu, who served as China's premier from 1998 to 2003, is remembered as one of the country's most important economic reformers.

While hailing the late premier as a "loyal" party member, the Chinese state is also wary that public mourning for his era of reform can easily turn into veiled criticisms of the current government under Xi.

Xi was among the leaders who had visited Zhu in hospital or sent condolences after his death, Chinese state media reported on Tuesday. Others included incumbent premier Li Qiang and ex-president Hu Jintao.

After his death, state media described Zhu as an "outstanding member of the Chinese Communist Party" and a "time-tested and loyal Communist fighter".

He was cremated at Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery, an exclusive resting place for high-ranking officials and other prominent figures.

Meanwhile, online, posts about Zhu have been contained and censored - including an essay written by economist Zhao Jian, which remembered Zhu's era as a time when people were "properly poor" but saw a clear future ahead.

"There were no smartphones then, no short-form videos and no screens filled by the purveyors of anxiety," he wrote.

"The sky was blue, life moved slowly and people could say what they really thought."

The party has long been fearful of public reaction to deaths of senior officials and public figures.

The deaths of former premier Zhou Enlai in 1976 and former CCP general secretary Hu Yaobang in 1989 prompted widespread outpourings of grief that morphed into protests.

Zhu died just days before the Communist Party leadership gathered to commemorate the birth centenary of President Jiang Zemin, who died in 2022.

The death of Zhu and Jiang, two prominent leaders from the same era, has prompted a wave of nostalgia among many Chinese people for a time when the country looked as if it was going in a different direction - when it appeared that it may open to the world and allow more freedom for its people.

Previously purged under Mao Zedong's regime, Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death in 1976.

Zhu served as premier alongside Jiang Zemin, who became Communist Party chief in 1989 and president in 1993.

The two men served alongside each other at the top of China's leadership from 1998 to 2003, leading China through an era of rapid economic growth and entry into global trade.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns

summary.en: Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

title.en: A fake website and a deluge of CVs: the Australian firm embroiled in an FBI probe into alleged Chinese espionage

summary.en: An Australian firm has been caught up in an FBI investigation into alleged Chinese espionage, involving a fake consultancy website that impersonated the Brisbane company. This fake site was among 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice.

body.en: Exclusive: Fake consultancy impersonating Brisbane firm online is one of 13 websites seized by the US Department of Justice Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast When the first emails arrived, they were easily dismissed as spam. But as strangers continued to boast about their defence and security credentials, they became impossible to ignore. From mid-2025, a small Australian consultancy firm called Horizzen started receiving emails and strange calls from people applying for vague jobs in the United States. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：在线冒充布里斯班公司的虚假咨询公司是美国司法部查获的 13 个网站之一 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客以获取最新更新 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 当第一批电子邮件到达时，它们很容易被视为垃圾邮件而被忽略。但随着陌生人继续吹嘘他们的国防和安全资历，他们变得不可能被忽视。从 2025 年中期开始，一家名为 Horizzen 的澳大利亚小型咨询公司开始收到人们在美国申请模糊工作的电子邮件和奇怪的电话。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights how deception, even when elaborately crafted, often has a limited lifespan. While falsehoods may initially mislead, their true nature is eventually revealed, as seen in the seizure of these fake websites. Yahweh's word reminds us that truth ultimately prevails, and deceit cannot endure indefinitely.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了欺骗，即使精心策划，也往往寿命有限。虚假信息可能一时蒙蔽，但其真实面目终将被揭露，正如这些虚假网站被查获一样。雅伟的话语提醒我们，真理最终会得胜，谎言无法永远持续。

verse.textEn: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
verse.textZh: 口吐真言，永远坚立；舌说谎话，只存片时。

title.en: How to buy a ‘mega-dinghy’: the perilous new model of Channel crossing
title.zh: 如何购买“巨型橡皮艇”：危险的英吉利海峡偷渡新模式

summary.en: The Guardian China reports on the alarming trend of large dinghies, capable of carrying hundreds, being used for perilous Channel crossings. The article investigates the supply chain for these vessels, noting that large orders are readily fulfilled by manufacturers.
summary.zh: 《卫报》中国版报道称，载有数百人的大型充气艇被用于危险的英吉利海峡偷渡，这一趋势令人担忧。文章调查了这些大型船只的来源，指出制造商可以轻松满足大批量订单。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...
body.zh: 载有数百人的船只是一个明显且令人震惊的趋势。但这么大的船只从哪里来呢？他们表示，只要订单超过 20 艘，提供一艘在西欧波涛汹涌的海域使用的大型小艇就不成问题。这家中国公司的销售经理甚至还为一位冒充潜在客户的卫报卧底记者准备了一份在线手册供其细读。他们的生产能力为每月 500 艘船，是的，有可能以合适的价格获得更大的船。他们可以以每艘 1,678 美元（1,238 英镑）的价格制造一艘七米甚至八米长的军用小艇，不带发动机，但这将缺乏 CE 认证，这是表明产品符合欧盟健康和安全要求的强制性标志。林登·李的补充报道继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report on the supply of vessels for perilous journeys reminds us of the vulnerable individuals seeking safety and new beginnings. Yahweh calls us to recognize His presence in those who are marginalized and in desperate need. Our compassion for 'the least of these' reflects our love for Him.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于用于危险旅程的船只供应的报道，提醒我们那些寻求安全和新生活的弱势个体。雅伟呼召我们要在那些被边缘化和极度需要的人身上认出祂的存在。我们对“这些最小的弟兄”的怜悯，反映了我们对祂的爱。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: The Fauci hearing was painful to watch. But we need answers on Covid-19’s origin| David Relman
title.zh: 福奇听证会令人痛苦，但我们需要新冠病毒起源的答案 | 大卫·雷尔曼

summary.en: Despite recent congressional hearings, understanding the origin of Covid-19 remains elusive, with a microbiologist observing a deterioration in public discourse surrounding the issue.
summary.zh: 尽管近期国会举行了听证会，但了解新冠病毒的起源仍然困难重重，一位微生物学家指出，围绕这一问题的公共讨论正在恶化。

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. David Relman is a professor of medicine and microbiology at Stanford University. He was an inaugural member of the US National Science Advisory Board for Biosecurity and president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America Continue reading...
body.zh: 尽管最近在国会举行了听证会，但我们似乎距离了解 Covid-19 起源的目标比以往任何时候都更远。作为一名微生物学家和传染病临床医生，很难看到最近公众关于 Covid-19 起源的讨论的转移。对我来说，阅读安东尼·福奇在他现已公开的日记中关于起源争论的评论尤其困难。 7 月 29 日美国参议员兰德·保罗主持的电视节目对福奇进行敌意审讯，令人感到痛苦。尽管包括我自己在内的许多人早期呼吁对我们所知道、不知道和需要了解的 Covid-19 起源进行冷静、客观的评估，但我们现在似乎比以往任何时候都离这个目标更远——受到政治化、两极分化和不合逻辑思维的困扰。大卫·雷尔曼是斯坦福大学医学和微生物学教授。他是美国国家生物安全科学咨询委员会的首任成员和美国传染病学会主席继续阅读...

Proverbs 18:17 suggests that true understanding emerges only after hearing all sides and carefully scrutinizing every claim. This calls for patience and a commitment to truth beyond...

title.en: Pauline Hanson is targeting superannuation. Should it be easier to access your savings?

summary.en: Investment experts say early withdrawal can substantially reduce retirement funds, but they suggest reducing contribution rates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The superannuation system is Pauline Hanson’s latest target. The One Nation leader has made...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The One Nation leader has made it clear that her party backs looser rules around how Australians can access their retirement savings.

In a cost-of-living crisis, she argues it’s not right to force people to save for the future when they can’t make ends meet today.

“Some people, you know, who need these [medical] operations can’t get access to their superannuation to have that done,” Hanson claimed this week. “Superannuation should be lightened up a bit so people can utilise this money in times of crisis. It is their money.”

Jane Hume, the deputy Liberal leader, in response said the Coalition would revisit whether Australians should be able to get access to their retirement savings early - albeit for the narrower purpose of helping buy a first home.

Hume added: “I do think that superannuation is highly valued by Australians, it’s not something that you need in your working life, it’s something you need in your retired life.”

When asked, Jim Chalmers, the treasurer, has repeatedly pointed out that there are already ways for people to pull from their retirement for compassionate reasons or due to financial hardship.

According to the ATO, 63,300 individuals in 2024-25 were granted early access for compassionate reasons, the vast majority to pay for a medical treatment.

To put that into context, there are roughly 14 million people with at least one super account who are not past retirement age.

The sums were not trivial – more than $1.4bn was withdrawn early under compassionate grounds in that financial year. That suggests the average amount was about $22,400.

The total amount approved for early release for compassionate reasons is also climbing quickly. It was up about 40% on 2023-24, and was nearly double the $762m accessed in 2022-23, according to the ATO.

The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority reports the amount of early release of super payments for severe financial hardship. A little over $1bn was paid out to fund members under this category in 2024-25, and has also increased rapidly over recent years.

Jessica Spence, the director of policy at Super Consumers Australia, says there’s always room for improvement in the super system.

body.en:
Dozens of eleventh-hour amendments to a controversial bill designed to claw back runaway disability spending have passed the upper house despite outcry from advocates.

Labor has been touting changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme, including sweeping new powers for the relevant minister and a cut in social funding, since April in a bid to save $37.8 billion by the end of the decade.

The changes passed the Senate on Tuesday night, with 28 in favour and 12 against.

But just hours before a final vote on the bill was due to take place, the government unveiled 63 changes in response to community concern.

Under one change, severely disabled Australians who require constant care will be able to appeal decisions made by the NDIS minister that affect their funding.

Participants can request a variation to their plan for specific sections, including assistance with daily living.

Community and social participation funding, which is set to be slashed despite its role in helping disabled people access friends, appointments and work, will remain ineligible for appeal.

The changes to the scheme would take away a lifeline for thousands of Australians, Greens disability spokesperson Jordon Steele-John said.

"Labor and the Liberals got together in a room, and they decided to strip us of our rights, regardless of our safety and dignity," said Steele-John, who lives with a disability.

Increased penalties for NDIS providers benefiting from kickbacks have been included in the changes, along with specific whistleblower protections.

"There will be tough new aggravated integrity offences, including obtaining funds by deception, providing false or misleading information for abuse of position as a participant's nominee, or for intentionally destroying records," NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister told reporters before the amendments were voted on.

The changes passed the upper house on Tuesday night with little debate, following a deal struck with the coalition for the removal of a so-called widow tax hidden in the federal government's budget reforms.

In exchange for closing the loophole, which would have caused divorcees and widows to lose negative gearing entitlements on investment properties, the opposition will support Labor's bill.

The conflation of the previously unrelated topics rendered disabled people a political football, Steele-John said.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers had announced Labor's plans to close the loophole weeks earlier, but the government was not planning to introduce it to parliament until later in 2026, with consultation on the draft bill not due to end until Friday.

body.en:
Contentious gambling reforms, including restrictions on incentives and a national register to opt out of online gambling ads, are set to pass after Labor and the Coalition struck a deal.

The Labor caucus approved the deal on Tuesday morning, after the government made several amendments to secure Coalition support.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the reforms would protect those most at risk of harm.

"Australians will be better protected from inducements and direct marketing," he told parliament.

But gambling reform advocates have been critical of the bill, which was passed in the lower house with 96 votes to nine. It will be debated in the upper house and is expected to be passed this week.

Among them were two Coalition MPs — Pat Conaghan and Andrew Wallace — who crossed the floor and joined the independents to vote against the laws. Both have spoken out, saying the laws don't go far enough.

"I don't like gambling. The reality is $36 billion is lost on gambling each and every single year. That's $95 million a day that is lost to gambling in Australia," Wallace told News24.

"I've never crossed the floor in 10 years in my parliamentary career but I've just heard too many stories of my constituents and people across Australia who have lost everything, who have sometimes lost their lives."

The agreement between the government and Opposition means the Coalition will also support changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) in exchange for Labor expediting a push to remove a so-called widow's tax which was part of tax changes in the May budget.

Communications Minister Anika Wells said the government had listened to the community and taken steps to address the "most toxic version of inducements".

"The reforms introduced to parliament represent the most significant reforms to online gambling in Australia’s history," she said.

"This package of reforms minimises children’s exposure to wagering advertising, takes action on predatory inducements and cracks down on illegal gambling operators."

Opposition communications spokesperson Sarah Henderson claimed the amendments were a win for the Coalition.

"Labor's bill simply did not go far enough to protect children and vulnerable Australians," she said.

The gambling reforms are the first in the three years since a landmark report by late Labor MP Peta Murphy , who called for a total phase-out of gambling ads.

A Senate committee report on the proposed changes was tabled on Monday night, criticising the government's reforms as being too little, too late.

summary.en: One Nation's proposal to lower cigarette prices aims to curb the black market, but experts are debating whether this could undermine decades of public health efforts against smoking.

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has vowed to slash the tax on tobacco by 75 per cent and dramatically reduce the price of legal cigarettes, arguing the move would curb the booming black market.

Illicit tobacco trade in Australia has expanded rapidly since 2020. The value of illicit tobacco attempting to enter the market has soared from $1.74 billion in 2018-19 to more than $6.4 billion in 2023-24, according to Australian Taxation Office estimates.

Meanwhile, government revenue from the tobacco excise — the tax applied to legal tobacco products — has plummeted and is forecast to continue declining.

"Labor has not only lost the revenue, it has lost control of the black market in illegal tobacco," Hanson said in her announcement on Tuesday.

body.en:
Sydney Swans coach Dean Cox says he's "extremely disappointed" after several players were linked to a police investigation into an alleged sexual assault.

Victoria Police attended the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne on Monday to investigate a sexual assault report in the early hours of the morning.

The Sydney Swans were staying at the hotel, having defeated Essendon at the nearby Melbourne Cricket Ground on Sunday night.

The win meant they locked in second place on the AFL ladder, guaranteeing they would play two home finals, with only an inconsequential game against 13th-placed North Melbourne remaining to complete their home-and-away season.

SBS News has chosen not to name the players as it has not independently verified their identities.

Victoria Police issued a brief statement, confirming it was investigating a sexual assault report and the "exact circumstances are yet to be established and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing".

On Tuesday morning, coach Dean Cox briefly spoke to reporters outside of the Swans' Sydney headquarters for the first time since the news broke.

"Obviously extremely disappointed with what's happened, and understand the questions and we'll update as we gather more information," Cox said.

Asked if player sanctions could be expected, Cox said: "We're working our way through everything with the AFL and the relevant parties and we'll update when we get more information."

He was also asked whether he had spoken to the players involved, saying: "We'll speak as the day unfolds."

Co-captain Callum Mills also spoke briefly to waiting media at Moore Park on Tuesday morning as he and other players started to filter into the club.

"I can't really comment. There's an investigation ongoing and we don't have the facts yet," Mills said.

The group of players reportedly drove back to Sydney from Melbourne on Monday night.

title.en: Women’s physical and mental health 'inseparable', new endometreosis research finds
title.zh: 新子宫内膜异位症研究发现女性身心健康“密不可分”

summary.en: New research has identified a significant deficiency in Australia's women's healthcare system, revealing the critical link between women's physical and mental health, particularly concerning conditions like endometriosis.
summary.zh: 新研究发现澳大利亚女性医疗保健系统存在巨大缺陷，揭示了女性身心健康之间密不可分的联系，尤其是在子宫内膜异位症等疾病方面。

body.en:
Women living with endometriosis, ovarian cysts and hormone-related conditions are experiencing significantly higher rates of anxiety, depression and self-harm, highlighting the need for mental health support to be integrated into women’s physical healthcare.

Research published by Women's Mental Health Australia on Tuesday found almost half of women with endometriosis reported experiencing anxiety.

Women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome experienced depression and anxiety at up to twice the rate of women without the condition.

The findings have uncovered major gaps in Australia's healthcare system, according to chief operating officer Katrina Locandro.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"The government's investing a lot in women's health at the moment ... and there is a really practical step that they could be taking to reduce that gap."

The findings indicate that physical health conditions are associated with poorer mental health.

But the greatest psychological toll is on women living with female-specific physical health conditions, including polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, a broad condition involving a hormone imbalance, irregular periods and ovarian cysts.

Women with that syndrome reported high rates of depression and anxiety, between 1.6 and 2.2 times higher than women who did not have the condition.

The disparity also extended to suicide and self-harm rates, reported by 10 per cent of women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome and 13 per cent of women with endometriosis, compared with four per cent of women without those conditions.

The research found that one in three women are not seeking help for their mental health issues, often because of financial and stigma-related reasons.

Locandro says every woman attending a government-funded endometriosis and pelvic pain clinic should receive an integrated mental health assessment and support as a standard offering.

"We're not asking the government to build a new system, we're asking it to strengthen an existing one by recognising that women's physical and mental health are inseparable," she said.

Report co-author Bronwyn Graham said that embedding integrated mental health assessment and support into existing services would be a game-changer.

"Women are being asked to manage two separate journeys, one for their body and one for their mind, and to find their own way between them at the point they are least able to."
